Ratio of pipeline route length to the great circle distance between the centers of the two states. The length scales the compressor fuel and leakage losses of the pipeline.

Whether the existing natural gas infrastructure may retire, by part. A part that may retire is optimised between zero and its existing capacity, so assets whose fixed O&M outweighs their value retire; their sunk investment is not counted. Retrofitting to hydrogen (``retrofit``) does not need it: a part that may not retire keeps its existing capacity, as natural gas or retrofitted. Trade pipelines and linepack stay fixed.
Gas production.
Pipelines between states.

Underground storage (store, injection and withdrawal). Whenever a storage retires or is retrofitted, its withdrawal keeps the share of its existing capacity that its store keeps, and its injection at least that share and at most its withdrawal.

Natural gas infrastructure retrofitted to hydrogen in the first investment period, with the hydrogen sector (``E-G-H``). The model optimizes how much of the existing capacity to retrofit, from zero to all. What is retrofitted is taken from the natural gas capacity: the gas left plus the hydrogen capacity over its conversion factor is the existing gas capacity, or at most it if the part may also retire (``economic_retirement``). See :ref:`data-hydrogen`.
Allow retrofitting the natural gas pipelines between states.
Allow retrofitting salt dome, depleted field and aquifer gas storage. With ``storage_aggregation: state``, a state's storage takes the mean costs and conversion factors of its formations.
How underground storage reservoirs are aggregated. ``state`` builds one storage per state; ``formation`` builds one per state and formation (depleted field, aquifer, salt dome).
Options of methane emission accounting attached to natural gas networks
Upstream per_unit leakage rate of natural gas. Applied to gas processing facilities.
Downstream per_unit leakage rate of natural gas. Applied to all end-use technologies that use natural gas.
Global warming potential of methane. GWP of 1 represents same carbon intensity as burned natural gas.
